py-dict.def: A collection of key: value pairs, looked up by key: car["mpg"]. Keys are unique.

py-set.def: An unordered collection with no duplicates: set([3, 1, 3]) is {1, 3}.

py-tuple.def: A fixed, unchangeable group of values in round brackets, e.g. a point (3, 4) or an array shape.

py-unpack.def: Catching the parts of a tuple or list in several names at once: x, y = (3, 4).

py-while.def: Repeats a block as long as a condition is true; something inside must eventually make it false.

py-enumerate.def: enumerate(xs) gives (index, item) pairs for a loop.

py-zip.def: zip(a, b) pairs items position by position, stopping at the shorter input.

py-comprehension.def: A one-line way to build a list or dict: [x ** 2 for x in xs if x > 0].

py-scope.def: Where a name exists. Names assigned inside a function are local to it and vanish when it returns.

py-lambda.def: A one-line nameless function, e.g. lambda p: p[1]; often used as a key= for sorting.

py-class.def: A blueprint for objects that bundle data (attributes, set in __init__ on self) with functions (methods).

py-knn.def: Classify a new point by the majority class of the \(k\) closest training points (or average their values, for regression).
